content.text: Why This Infrastructure Works When Platforms Fail: Ebooks kenya

The problem with platforms like Stripe and Amazon is that they centralize control and charge exorbitant fees. But with a sovereign ecommerce stack, you can create your own payment and delivery pipeline, using Cloudflare and NOWPayments. This infrastructure is built on open-source technologies, like GitHub Pages, Cloudflare Workers, and Supabase, which are free to use and give you complete control over your data. By deploying this stack, you can process transactions in under 60 seconds, with fees under $0.10, using USDT on Tron. And with Binance P2P, you can accept payments in Kenyan shillings, naira, and cedis. This is the future of ecommerce, and it's available to everyone, regardless of where they're from.
What You Need Before You Deploy

Before you can deploy a sovereign ecommerce stack, you'll need a few things. First, you'll need to create a Cloudflare account and set up a GitHub Pages site. Next, you'll need to create a NOWPayments account and set up a payment address. You'll also need to choose a cryptocurrency to use for payments, like USDT on Tron. And finally, you'll need to create a Supabase account to store your order data. With these tools in place, you'll be ready to deploy your stack.
Setting Up Your Payment and Delivery Pipeline

Once you have your accounts set up, it's time to configure your payment and delivery pipeline. This involves setting up a Cloudflare Worker to handle incoming payments, and a Supabase table to store your order data. You'll also need to set up a file delivery pipeline using Cloudflare R2, so that you can deliver your ebooks to customers automatically. And finally, you'll need to configure your NOWPayments account to accept payments in your local currency, like Kenyan shillings.
You can accept payments in Kenyan shillings, naira, and cedis using Binance P2P and USDT on Tron.
Going Live and Processing Your First Transaction

With your payment and delivery pipeline set up, it's time to go live and process your first transaction. First, you'll need to test your stack by sending a small payment to your NOWPayments address. Then, you'll need to configure your Cloudflare Worker to send a webhook to your Supabase table, so that you can store the order data. Finally, you'll need to deliver your ebook to the customer using Cloudflare R2. With these steps complete, you'll be able to process transactions in under 60 seconds, with fees under $0.10.
Scaling Once the Infrastructure Is Running

Once your infrastructure is running smoothly, it's time to scale. This involves configuring your Cloudflare account to handle increased traffic, and setting up a load balancer to distribute traffic across multiple instances. You'll also need to configure your Supabase account to handle increased order volume, and set up a backup system to ensure that your data is safe. With these steps complete, you'll be able to handle large volumes of traffic and sales, without ever needing to rely on a central platform.
